stances_toward.note: Kenya's DRC file is the Nairobi process, and it is shrinking. Uhuru Kenyatta facilitated the EAC track from Nairobi; the EAC-SADC summit of February 2025 merged it with the Luanda process, Kenyatta complained that Nairobi had been 'sidelined' and the EACRF withdrawal slowed talks; then Washington (accords between Kinshasa and Kigali, signed on 4 December 2025) and Doha (the Kinshasa-AFC/M23 framework of November 2025) took the lead, and Mudavadi welcomed the Qatari-brokered deal in 2025. Partner (EAC co-member) and not rival: Nairobi has no quarrel with Kinshasa, only a diminishing role. Cooling because Kenya's centrality is contested by the other tracks. Confidence C: no source grades the pair. Bond none. Gap: Kabila's and the AFC's relations with Nairobi were not sourced.

stances_toward.note: Rival, not adversary - argued both ways. For adversary: the RDF fights inside the DRC (UN experts: 3,000-4,000 troops in 2024, command and control over M23, a 'final objective' of territory and resources), took Goma, Bukavu and Uvira with AFC/M23, the US sanctioned Kabarebe (20 Feb 2025) and the RDF (2 Mar 2026), and Kigali treats Kinshasa's links with the FDLR as its casus belli. Against: the grade follows structure and no declared aim is the end of the Congolese state or of Tshisekedi's regime - Kigali's stated aim is the FDLR and a security zone on its border, it signed the Washington peace agreement (27 Jun 2025) and the Accords (4 Dec 2025, with an economic integration framework), and its foreign ministry asks for their full implementation and for the Doha annexes to be concluded (10 Dec 2025); Kinshasa signed the same texts and seeks withdrawal, not Kigali's destruction. State of play, 13 Oct 2026: the US asked both sides to hold the ceasefire and stop drone strikes, demanded 'immediate and unconditional' Rwandan withdrawal and faster Congolese action on the FDLR (120+ repatriated), welcomed a 15-detainee exchange with AFC/M23 and called for the outstanding Doha protocols; AFC/M23 left Uvira by Feb 2026 and parts of the Sange area in May 2026; Rwanda and the DRC announced de-escalation steps in Mar 2026; Kagame (Apr 2026) refuses to lift the 'defensive measures'. No source uses the word 'rival': structural reading, confidence B because the underlying facts are tier 1-2. Bond grievance: 1994, the refugee camps and the wars of 1996-2003.

stances_toward.note: Partner, cooling: our reading (confidence C). Tanzania sent troops to the SADC mission in eastern DRC (SAMIDRC, deployed December 2023). SADC leaders ended the mandate on 13 March 2025 after M23 took Goma, and the phased withdrawal began on 29 April 2025 (Daily Maverick, Africanews). Not hostile: the DRC is the largest user of the Dar es Salaam transit route, 7.77m tonnes of 14.61m in 2025/26 (about 53%; Tanzanian government figures as reported, the share is our arithmetic). The withdrawal cools a commitment; it is not a dispute.

stances_toward.note: Kinshasa agreed to Operation Shujaa with the UPDF from November 2021, so the two cooperate against the ADF out of necessity. Uganda resists alignment: the ICJ ordered it to pay USD 325m in reparations for its 1998-2003 occupation (judgment of 9 February 2022, payable in five USD 65m instalments; the first was paid in September 2022). Later instalments, due to 1 September 2026, are not verified. The UN experts say Ugandan units shielded M23 (July 2025 report as reported); Uganda denies it. reluctant_partner is our reading of that structure, not a source's word. Bond grievance: the ICJ case is an open wound. Gap: whether the 2026 instalments were paid.
